--confirm.description: Step 3: the user approved the ruling (never add this on your own initiative). Refused unless the read was confirmed first

--receipt.description: Read receipt(s) from the previous step's envelope (its confirmCommand carries them — a bare token for one crossing, <id>=<token>,… for a batch); required with --confirm-read (stage 1) and --confirm (stage 2), verified server-side per crossing

--task.description: Task the crossing belongs to (defaults to the session-bound task)

crossing disposition.description: Rule on one or more boundary crossings from the terminal (LUM-769; several ids = one batch per ruling, LUM-845 — each step prints ONE envelope listing every crossing in full and carrying one receipt per crossing as --receipt <id>=<token>,…; drop an id between steps to leave that crossing OPEN; every write is reported per crossing) through a three-step confirmation handshake the server enforces: (1) no step flag — prints the crossing (severity, detail, agent explanations) as an envelope with a stage-1 read receipt, exit 4, writes nothing; (2) --confirm-read --receipt <r1> after the user confirms they READ it — returns the stage-2 receipt and a second envelope for the ruling, exit 4; (3) --confirm --receipt <r2> after the user approves the ruling — writes. Confirming before the read is acknowledged is refused and told to confirm the read first. Relay each envelope; never supply a step flag yourself. Either ruling clears the crossing's block on DONE and is audited as a CLI-channel disposition. Reverting to OPEN and repository suppression rules stay web-only. Targets a crossing on the session-bound task unless --task is given.

--file.description: Batch: a JSON array of {"id": "<crossing>", "note": "<text>"} — one note per crossing, in one call; "-" reads stdin. Replaces <id> --note

--note.description: The explanation to record (the rationale for the action / why it may be a false positive); required with <id>

--task.description: Task the crossing belongs to (defaults to the session-bound task; unattached sessions must pass it)

crossing explain.description: Append an agent self-explanation ("申辩") to a boundary crossing (LUM-542). Append-only and for the human reviewer — it never clears the crossing or unblocks Done (a human dispositions that). Several crossings in one call: --file with a JSON array of {"id","note"} (LUM-845); each is reported. Targets crossings on the session-bound task.

Requires the doc to have a stored markdown source. Commits conditionally on the body revision: a concurrent edit fails with 409 instead of being overwritten. A replacement that drops tables/rows/headings within the addressed section is rejected with 422 (structure guard) unless --allow-shrink is passed.

doc rebuild-source.description: Regenerate the stored markdown source from the doc's HTML body using a lossless serializer (tables/rows/headings round-trip), re-enabling doc show --raw / diff / patch / append for a source-less doc. The rebuilt source is structure-guarded: any table/tr/heading shrink is rejected with 422 (no silent flattening) unless --allow-shrink is passed. A doc that already has a source is refused with 409 unless --force re-derives it (replacing a byte-faithful source with a serializer-derived one).

--agent.description: Set up only this agent (claude-code, codex, cursor, gemini-cli, github-copilot, windsurf). Baked into every hook command; codex installs the Codex skill layout, .codex/hooks.json and .codex/rules/lumo.rules, the others the Claude Code layout. init.description: Set up Lumo for Claude Code and Codex together: the skill into .claude/skills/ and .agents/skills/, hook handlers into .claude/settings.json and .codex/hooks.json (which you then trust in Codex /hooks), and a Codex rule (.codex/rules/lumo.rules) that lets `lumo` commands reach the Lumo API from Codex's sandbox. --agent <token> sets up just that agent. Run via `npx @lumoai/cli init` for first-time onboarding; `lumo init --upgrade` refreshes existing installs.

report.description: Summarize token usage and tasks completed over a window of local days (default: last 7 days incl. today). Team totals plus a per-member split; --member me for just yourself

--no-worktree.description: Do not create a worktree even when .lumo/worktree.json sets autoWorktree

--steward.description: Bind as a STEWARD (governance) session to a milestone (id, name, or slug) instead of a task. Steward sessions plan and accept only: self-dispatch to in_progress is refused, and implementation commits/PRs are recorded as boundary crossings.

--worktree.description: Create this task's worktree under .worktrees/ when none exists (LUM-825; only from the main checkout; failures never fail attach). Default: .lumo/worktree.json autoWorktree, else off.

session attach.description: Attach the current Claude Code or Codex session to a task — or, with --steward, to a MILESTONE as a governance session (LUM-640: plan/accept only). Either binding is a lifetime lock: re-attaching the same target is a no-op, anything else is refused — start a new session instead.

session status.description: Show what the current Claude Code or Codex session is bound to: a task, a milestone (STEWARD governance session), or nothing.

--agent.description: Set up only this agent (claude-code, codex, cursor, gemini-cli, github-copilot, windsurf). Baked into every hook command; codex installs the Codex skill layout, .codex/hooks.json and .codex/rules/lumo.rules, the others the Claude Code layout. Without it, init sets up claude-code and codex.

--force.description: Overwrite existing skill files (SKILL.md + references/) even when they were modified locally, and a .codex/rules/lumo.rules Lumo did not write

--project.description: Install into ./.claude and ./.agents + ./.codex (applies to the current project only)

--upgrade.description: Upgrade every known Lumo install (no scope prompt): managed, older skill copies are replaced; modified or newer copies are skipped; Codex hooks.json is rewritten only when the Lumo event set changed (then re-trust in Codex /hooks); a recorded Lumo Codex rule is refreshed when it differs

--user.description: Install into ~/.claude and ~/.agents + ~/.codex (applies across all projects for this user)

setup.description: Alias of `lumo init` (kept for older docs and scripts).

sprint add.description: Add a task to a sprint. <task> accepts LUM-N or UUID.

--backlog-all.description: Return all unfinished tasks to the backlog

--confirm.description: The user has approved the change shown in the confirmation envelope (LUM-755). Without it the command exits 4 and prints what it would do.

--move-all.description: Move all unfinished tasks to the next sprint

sprint close.description: Close an ACTIVE sprint. With no unfinished tasks, closes immediately. Pass --move-all to move unfinished tasks to the next sprint, or --backlog-all to return them to the backlog; either mode without --confirm exits 4 with a confirmation envelope listing the tasks that would move.

--name.description: Sprint name (server fills default when omitted)

sprint create.description: Create a draft sprint. --team required when workspace has >1 team. --start and --end (YYYY-MM-DD) required.

--confirm.description: The user has approved the change shown in the confirmation envelope (LUM-755). Without it the command exits 4 and prints what it would do.

sprint delete.description: Delete a DRAFT sprint. Without --confirm: exit 4 + a confirmation envelope with the task count. Server rejects ACTIVE/CLOSED sprints.

--limit.description: Show only the first N sprints

--status.description: Filter by status: draft | active | closed (case-insensitive)

sprint list.description: List sprints for a team. --team required when workspace has >1 team. Sorted newest first.

sprint remove.description: Remove a task from a sprint. <task> accepts LUM-N or UUID.

--team.description: Team name or UUID (when workspace has >1 team)

sprint show.description: Show a sprint: status, dates, progress, and tasks. Identifier accepts a sprint number or UUID.

sprint start.description: Transition a DRAFT sprint to ACTIVE.

--team.description: Team name or UUID (when workspace has >1 team)

sprint summary.description: Show the AI-generated summary for a sprint. Identifier accepts a sprint number or UUID. Prints "(no summary generated yet)" when none exists. Use --retry to queue regeneration before fetching.

--team.description: Team name or UUID (when workspace has >1 team)

sprint update.description: Update a sprint. Provide at least one of --name, --start, --end. Identifier accepts a sprint number or UUID. Empty strings are rejected — these fields cannot be cleared.

tag create.description: Create a tag (≤30 chars). A duplicate name is refused (409). To tag a task, use `task update --add-tag`.

tag list.description: List workspace tags with their color and how many tasks / docs carry each.

task artifact.description: Record spec-engineering artifacts (spec / plan / design …) on a task

--agent.description: Coding tool that produced the artifact: claude-code | codex | cursor | gemini-cli | github-copilot | windsurf (case-insensitive)

--file.description: File whose contents become the artifact body

--kind.description: Artifact kind, e.g. spec | plan | design (opaque)

--source.description: Spec-gen framework, formal name e.g. Superpowers | "Spec Kit" | BMad | OpenSpec | GSD (opaque; quote names with spaces)

task artifact add.description: Attach an artifact to a task. --kind/--title/--source are stored verbatim; --file supplies the content.

task artifact list.description: List artifacts attached to a task, in order

--confirm.description: The user has approved the change shown in the confirmation envelope (LUM-755). Without it the command exits 4 and prints what it would do.

task artifact rm.description: Delete an artifact from a task (irreversible). Without --confirm: exit 4 + a confirmation envelope naming the artifact.

task artifact show.description: Show one artifact (key:value header + content body). Find <artifact-id> in `artifact list` column 1.

--agent.description: New coding tool: claude-code | codex | cursor | gemini-cli | github-copilot | windsurf (case-insensitive)

--source.description: New spec-gen framework, formal name e.g. Superpowers | "Spec Kit" | BMad | OpenSpec | GSD (quote names with spaces)

task artifact update.description: Update an artifact’s kind / title / source (not content). Provide at least one flag.

--reply-to.description: Reply to a top-level comment: its #id from `task comments list` (unique prefix of 6+ chars)

task comment.description: Add a comment to a task. Body is plain text — quote it to pass spaces or newlines.

task comments.description: Read and manage the task comment thread

task comments edit.description: Replace the text of one of your own comments. <comment> is its #id from `task comments list` (unique prefix of 6+ chars).

--full.description: Print every comment, bypassing the output-token cap

task comments list.description: List the task comment thread (capped to the output budget; --full prints every comment)

--confirm.description: The user has approved the deletion shown in the confirmation envelope. Without it the command exits 4 and deletes nothing.

task comments rm.description: Delete one of your own comments (soft delete; replies under it are hidden too). Without --confirm: exit 4 + a confirmation envelope quoting the comment.

--full.description: Print full memory bodies and the judged-used track-record footer instead of the one-line index

task context.description: Print a task + prior session summaries as markdown, for pasting into a coding agent on startup. Memory prints one headline per item (full card: lumo memory show <id>).

--new-scope.description: Declare this is genuinely new work, outside your current task’s scope

--priority.description: Priority: low | medium | high | urgent (case-insensitive; default: low)

--project.description: Project name or slug

--rework-of.description: Declare this is rework of an existing task (redirects you to fix it; creates nothing)

--sprint.description: Sprint number or UUID to add the task to after creation

--template.description: Pre-fill the description from a task template (see `task template list`); not with --description

task create.description: Create a task. --project required when workspace has >1 project; defaults: priority=low, assignee=me.

task decide.description: Append a dated ruling to the task description's `## Decisions` section (created if missing). Use for decisions instead of comments.

--confirm.description: The user has approved the deletion shown in the confirmation envelope. Without it the command exits 4 and deletes nothing.

task delete.description: Move a task and all its subtasks to the trash (restorable for 30 days from web Settings → Trash, then permanently deleted). Without --confirm: exit 4 + a confirmation envelope listing what goes with it.

task deps.description: Task dependency edges — detected candidates + confirmed blockers

--confirm.description: The user has approved the change shown in the confirmation envelope (LUM-755). Without it the command exits 4 and prints what it would do.

task deps rm.description: Delete a dependency edge. Without --confirm: exit 4 + a confirmation envelope describing the edge.

task figma.description: Attach Figma file/frame links to a task

task figma add.description: Attach a Figma file or frame URL to the given task. Fetches file/frame name + thumbnail via Figma OAuth.

task figma context.description: Show the cached Figma design context (metadata)

task figma list.description: List Figma links attached to a task

task figma refresh.description: Re-fetch Figma metadata + thumbnail for every link on this task. Per-link failures isolated.

task figma rm.description: Remove a Figma link from a task (idempotent)

--json.description: Emit the raw activity entries as JSON

task history.description: Show the task field-change history (status, priority, title, assignee, due, tags, sprint), oldest first.

task lineage.description: Show the causal trail: which context fragments fed this task, each fragment's outcome, and the token/loop cost of the run that consumed it

--limit.description: Show only the first N tasks

--milestone.description: Filter by milestone name or UUID (scopes to my tasks under that milestone)

--project.description: Filter by project name (case-insensitive)

--status.description: Filter by status: backlog | todo | in_progress | in_review | done (case-insensitive)

task list.description: List tasks assigned to you. Filter with --status, --project, --milestone, --limit.

task memory.description: View and record memories scoped to a task

--agent.description: Producing agent: claude-code | codex | cursor | gemini-cli | github-copilot | windsurf (case-insensitive; default claude-code)

--trigger.description: trap/procedural: the situation that triggers it

task memory add.description: Record a memory on a task (<task> defaults to the bound session). Record only knowledge invisible in the codebase (the why, a runtime gotcha, a non-obvious failure, a non-trivial workflow); skip routine work. Pick --category then its fields.

--limit.description: Cap output to the first N rows

task memory list.description: List a task's memories. <task> defaults to the session-bound task.

task pr show.description: Show the synced PR record (diff/review comments when available)

--assignee.description: Assignee — me, an email, a member or agent name, or none for unassigned; repeatable (ORed)

--due-after.description: Due on or after YYYY-MM-DD (your local day)

--due-before.description: Due on or before YYYY-MM-DD (your local day)

--exact.description: Substring matching only, in board order (default: typo-tolerant, ranked by relevance)

--json.description: Emit the raw result as JSON

--limit.description: Show only the first N tasks

--priority.description: Priority: low | medium | high | urgent (case-insensitive; repeatable or comma-separated)

--project.description: Project name or slug

--status.description: Status: backlog | todo | in_progress | in_review | done (case-insensitive; repeatable or comma-separated)

task search.description: Search tasks across the whole workspace (any assignee). [query] terms must all match title/description (or a task number like LUM-42); typo-tolerant and ranked by relevance unless --exact. Every filter is applied server-side.

task show.description: Show a single task: title, status, priority, assignee, project, URL, description.

task slack show.description: Show the full stored Slack thread snapshot

--full.description: Also print the dashboard sections: cost, struggle/rework trail, trend

--json.description: Emit the versioned machine-readable payload (version field; breaking changes bump it)

task status.description: Task self-check (LUM-344): nextActions (undispositioned security findings + test-case advisories), security-scan coverage, and open boundary crossings. Read-only, no LLM. Defaults to the session-bound task. Run it first when resuming a task. --full adds the dashboard sections (cost, struggle/rework trail, trend).

task statuses.description: Show the task status set, allowed transitions and priorities, as served by the API.

task template.description: Task templates that pre-fill a new task description

--file.description: UTF-8 Markdown file with the template body (required, ≤20,000 chars); `-` reads stdin

task template create.description: Create a workspace template from a local Markdown file (OWNER only). <key> is a lowercase slug; built-in keys are reserved.

--file.description: Replace the body with this UTF-8 Markdown file; `-` reads stdin

task template edit.description: Change a workspace template (OWNER only): new name, new body from a Markdown file, and/or a new key. Built-ins cannot be edited.

--json.description: Emit the templates (with their Markdown content) as JSON

task template list.description: List the task templates available to `task create --template <key>`: built-ins plus your workspace ones.

--confirm.description: The user has approved the change shown in the confirmation envelope (LUM-755). Without it the command exits 4 and prints what it would do.

task template rm.description: Delete a workspace template (OWNER only, irreversible). Without --confirm: exit 4 + a confirmation envelope naming it.

--json.description: Emit key, name, description, isSystem and content as JSON

task template show.description: Print one template's Markdown (built-in or workspace) — redirect to save it: `show agent-brief > brief.md`.

task testcase.description: Structured test cases on a task (setup / steps / verification / expected) and their run records

--requires-env.description: local | preview | production (case-insensitive) - this case only proves anything when run there; a PASS recorded elsewhere is capped to UNPROVEN. Matched exactly: there is no environment hierarchy

--setup.description: Preconditions, e.g. "The user is on the Dashboard."

--step.description: One execution step (repeatable, ordered). At least one is required.

--verify.description: One verification step (repeatable, ordered). May be omitted entirely.

task testcase add.description: Add a test case. --step / --verify are repeatable and keep the order they appear in.

--confirm.description: Step 3 — THE USER's approval of the ruling. Never add this yourself.

--confirm-read.description: Step 2 — THE USER's confirmation that they read the envelope. Never add this yourself.

--known-defect.description: We accept this defect and ship anyway (does NOT claim it is fixed)

--not-a-defect.description: The failure was mis-attributed to the implementation

--receipt.description: The read receipt from the previous step of the handshake

task testcase disposition.description: Rule on a test case whose latest run proved an implementation defect — clears that run's block on DONE. Three-step handshake; never add a step flag yourself.

task testcase list.description: List a task's test cases with each one's latest run (result, environment, commit)

--confirm.description: The user has approved the change shown in the confirmation envelope (LUM-755). Without it the command exits 4 and prints what it would do.

task testcase rm.description: Remove a test case (soft delete - its run history stays readable). Without --confirm: exit 4 + a confirmation envelope.

--actual.description: What actually happened at the failing step (FAIL only), shown next to the expected result

--cause.description: Why it failed: defect | outdated | external | unknown (case-insensitive). REQUIRED on --result fail, refused otherwise. Only "defect" carries a burden of proof (needs at least one --evidence / --evidence-file); "unknown" is a real answer

--commit.description: Which commit this run exercised. Auto-detected from local git ONLY for --env local; required to record one for preview/production (the local checkout is not what they run)

--env.description: local | preview | production (case-insensitive; no default - say where this ran)

--evidence-file.description: Local file to upload as evidence: png/jpeg/webp/gif/txt/log/json, max 10 MB each, 5 files (repeatable)

--failed-step.description: 1-based index into the steps list (FAIL only; mutually exclusive with --failed-verify)

--failed-verify.description: 1-based index into the verification list (FAIL only; mutually exclusive with --failed-step)

--pr.description: The PR whose change this run exercised (must be linked to this task)

--step.description: Per-step result (repeatable): <step>=<result>[@duration], where <step> is s<n> for a step or v<n> for a verification check (ranges like s1-3) and <result> is pass or fail, e.g. s1-3=pass, v1=fail@0.3s. Steps you do not report are shown as "no per-step result", never as passed

--step-evidence.description: Attach evidence to one reported step (repeatable): s3=shot.png or v1=https://... Files count toward the 5-file limit

--unproven.description: 1-based index of a verification step this run could NOT observe (repeatable). A reported PASS that declares one is capped to UNPROVEN - you cannot pass on what you did not check

task testcase run.description: Record one execution. --env is REQUIRED and has no default - a run must say which environment it ran in.

task testcase show.description: Show one test case (four sections, 1-based step numbers) plus its run history. Handle: LUM-42/TC3

--requires-env.description: local | preview | production | none (case-insensitive) - this case only proves anything when run there; a PASS recorded elsewhere is capped to UNPROVEN. Pass "none" to clear it. Matched exactly: there is no environment hierarchy

--step.description: Replacement step (repeatable, ordered) - replaces the whole steps list

--verify.description: Replacement verification step (repeatable, ordered) - replaces the whole list

task testcase update.description: Edit a test case. --step / --verify REPLACE the whole list (they do not append). Provide at least one field.

--assignee.description: New assignee: email, name, or "me" (empty string to clear)

--claimable.description: Mark the task agent-claimable (surfaces in `lumo next --claimable`)

--confirm.description: With --status done: the user has approved the DONE transition shown in the confirmation envelope (LUM-755). Without it, --status done exits 4 and prints the envelope (status change, every linked PR, a ⚠ line for unmerged ones) instead of a prompt.

--due.description: Due date, YYYY-MM-DD (your local day); empty string to clear

--milestone.description: Milestone name (case-insensitive); empty string to unbind

--not-claimable.description: Mark the task NOT agent-claimable (mutually exclusive with --claimable)

--priority.description: New priority: low | medium | high | urgent (case-insensitive)

--remove-tag.description: Remove tag by name (repeatable). Unknown names are find-or-create, so prefer --remove-tag-id to avoid orphan rows.

--remove-tag-id.description: Remove tag by id (repeatable). Unknown ids are a no-op.

--sprint.description: Sprint number or UUID to bind the task to; empty string to unbind from current sprint

--status.description: New status: backlog | todo | in_progress | in_review | done (case-insensitive)

--tag.description: Set tags by name (bulk replace, repeatable)

--tag-id.description: Set tags by id (bulk replace, repeatable)

task update.description: Update a task. Provide at least one of --title, --description, --status, --priority, --assignee, --milestone, --sprint, or tag flags. Use "" to clear description, assignee, milestone, or sprint binding. --tag/--tag-id (bulk replace) cannot be combined with --add-tag/--add-tag-id/--remove-tag/--remove-tag-id.

task web show.description: Show the fetched web link body as plain text

task wrapup.description: Whole wrap-up in one read (LUM-841): test-case signals, security scans, open boundary crossings (each ready to relay, with the per-ruling disposition command), and DONE readiness with the DONE envelope preview (linked PR merge state + local worktree cleanup). Read-only: requests no receipt, changes no status. Defaults to the session-bound task.

--agent.description: Only installs of this agent (claude-code, codex, git, ...); the prepare-commit-msg hook is labelled git, so it is included only by --agent git

--confirm.description: Apply the removal after the user has approved the envelope

--force.description: Also delete skill copies that were edited locally (discards those edits)

--purge.description: Also delete everything in ~/.lumo (credentials, caches, install registry)

--scope.description: user (this machine), project (the current repo) or all (also recorded installs in other repos). Default: all

uninstall.description: Remove what `lumo init` installed: Lumo skill dirs, Lumo hook entries in Claude settings and Codex hooks.json (~/.codex or ./.codex), the Lumo Codex rule (.codex/rules/lumo.rules), the marked block in prepare-commit-msg, and the install registry records. Locally edited skill copies are skipped unless --force; foreign hooks and file content are kept. Without --confirm prints a confirmation envelope (exit 4) listing every path; never commits. Ends with the manual `npm rm -g @lumoai/cli` step.

--auto.description: Turn background auto-update on or off

update.description: Check npm for a newer @lumoai/cli and install it globally if available. The CLI also updates itself in the background by default; --auto on|off toggles that.

--apply.description: Write the corrections (default is a dry run)

--json.description: Print the merged server response as JSON

usage resync.description: Correct historical (inflated) token usage from local transcripts (LUM-932). Dry run by default — prints what would change; add --apply to write. Sends token counts only, never transcript content.

--full.description: Also print workspace name, key name and API URL

--json.description: Emit the identity as JSON (never includes the token)

whoami.description: Show the logged-in identity from local credentials (one line; no network call)

--ai-review.description: AI review (LLM security review and triage)

--confirm.description: The user approved turning the listed switches off

--disable-all.description: Turn every switch off at once

--enable-all.description: Turn every switch on at once

--json.description: Emit { switches, platform, effective } as JSON

--scan.description: Master switch: off = no layer runs, no PR comment

workspace security-scan.description: Show or change the PR security-scan switches (LUM-1002): the master scan switch, AI review and exploit-path hunt, with the platform ceiling and what actually runs. Any member may read; changing is OWNER only, and turning anything off exits 4 with a confirmation envelope until --confirm.

worktree.description: Scaffold, remove, list and prune per-task git worktrees under .worktrees/. Repo-specific links/copies/notes come from .lumo/worktree.json. Local dev tooling; run add/rm from the main checkout.

--base.description: Branch off this ref instead of the remote default branch (skips fetch)

--confirm.description: The user has seen and approved the verifyCommand shown in the confirmation envelope (LUM-755). Only meaningful with --verify.

--no-fetch.description: Do not fetch the remote default branch before branching

--verify.description: Run verifyCommand from .lumo/worktree.json in the new worktree to confirm a clean baseline. Without --confirm, exits 4 showing the exact command and creates nothing.

worktree add.description: Create a worktree at .worktrees/<LUM-N>[-slug] on branch lumo/<LUM-N>[-slug] off the remote default branch (origin/HEAD), link node_modules when present, copy the husky shim when husky owns hooks, and apply .lumo/worktree.json (linkPaths, copyPaths, notes). Run from the main checkout.

worktree list.description: List worktrees under .worktrees/: task id, branch, dirty state, and whether node_modules is symlinked.

--confirm.description: The user has approved the change shown in the confirmation envelope (LUM-755). Without it the command exits 4 and prints what it would do.

worktree prune.description: Remove the worktrees of tasks that are already DONE (closed on the web or another machine too). Keeps any worktree with uncommitted changes, commits that are neither pushed nor the head of a merged linked PR, or the current directory inside it. Without --confirm exits 4 with an envelope listing what goes and what stays. Never deletes branches.

--confirm.description: The user has approved the change shown in the confirmation envelope (LUM-755). Without it the command exits 4 and prints what it would do.

--delete-branch.description: Also delete the branch (git branch -d; refuses if unmerged)

--force.description: Remove even with uncommitted changes (discards them)

worktree rm.description: Remove the worktree for a task (git worktree remove). Without --confirm — or with uncommitted changes and no --force — exits 4 with a confirmation envelope naming the path, branch and what would be discarded. Keeps the branch unless --delete-branch.
